quote: How are you doing today? Got no form. I'm in got no form.
stewart_read: Rep's intro didn't anchor to a specific form detail before the customer denied it, so legitimacy was contested immediately.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did reference the form; the miss is procedural — no address/date specificity to back it up in the same breath.
coaching_implication: Lead with a specific detail (date filled, address) in the same sentence as the form reference to preempt denial.

quote: It our neighbor on the street has it.
stewart_read: Customer's neighbor-anecdote objection is a classic 'already have a bad reference point' — the schema calls for flipping the frame (their bill vs solar cost), but rep gave a flat replacement explanation instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep did attempt a version of the flip ('you would be paying more to the electric company') — this is a weak, not absent, flip attempt.
coaching_implication: Use the customer's own neighbor number if available, or pivot to 'what's your bill right now' immediately to make the comparison concrete instead of abstract.

quote: I mean, but I'm still paying for the panels and the solar energy if it's not my house.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same objection; rep restates the same abstract logic rather than escalating with a new angle or grounding it in the customer's own bill.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been strategically stalling to get to the bill question, which does land two lines later.
coaching_implication: Pull the bill number forward before re-arguing the objection — anchoring in their own $240 bill would have been sharper than repeating the general claim.

quote: They got panels all over the roof there and everything. And he still pays electric bill.
stewart_read: Third touch of the neighbor objection; rep asks a clarifying question ('is solar covering all his needs') instead of using it as a hook to build curiosity about the customer's own design.
alternative_hypothesis: The clarifying question could be a legitimate information-gathering move, not a miss — but it doesn't advance the call toward the customer's own numbers.
coaching_implication: Redirect immediately to the customer's own bill/usage rather than debating the neighbor's system specifics.

stewart_read: Bill amount is captured but the rep never reflects it back or ties it to savings before ending the call seconds later.
alternative_hypothesis: The call ended almost immediately after capture due to the utility DQ, so there was little time to use it — this is more a sequencing issue than a deliberate drop.
coaching_implication: Even a one-line acknowledgment ('$240, that's real money') before the DQ check would have preserved the anchor for any future contact.

quote: we we don't work with Valley Electric anyway. So I'll just take you off my list here. I appreciate your time.
stewart_read: Rep ends the call flatly on the utility gate without exploring an alternative path or softening the exit with any next step.
alternative_hypothesis: If Valley Electric is genuinely outside Ion's service area, ending the call is correct procedure, not a violation — the flat delivery is the only real gap.
coaching_implication: Even on a hard DQ, close with a courteous, specific reason so the customer doesn't feel dismissed after 3 minutes of friction.
